I'm planning JUnit 4 tests for SpyAnnotationEngine, covering the createMockFor method and the various branches of process: spying a plain instance, resetting an already-mocked instance, throwing when the instance is null, and handling conflicting @Spy/@Mock annotations.

Also considering edge cases like IllegalAccessException behavior with final fields, and sketching helper test classes with @Spy fields in different states (initialized, null, already-mocked, final).

For a static final field, I recall the doc specifies set access requires both setAccessible(true) and non-static, so static final fields always throw IllegalAccessException regardless of accessibility settings. That gives a concrete path to trigger the catch block, since the field isn't a mock and field.set() will fail, getting rethrown as a MockitoException with the "Problems initiating spied field" message — something I can verify in the test by checking both exception type and message.

Now I'm turning to testing the assertNoAnnotations method, which is package-private, so the test needs to live in the same package to access it.

I'm planning direct unit tests for this method: verifying it throws a MockitoException (from Reporter.unsupportedCombinationOfAnnotations) when conflicting annotations are present on a field, and passes cleanly when they aren't. I also want to cover edge cases — empty varargs for undesired annotations, an empty fields array, and specific annotation combos like @Spy with the deprecated @MockitoAnnotations.Mock, plus a @Captor combination.

I'm sketching out helper test classes with fields annotated differently (just @Mock, just @Captor, etc.) so I can call assertNoAnnotations directly with various undesired-annotation arguments and confirm the exception only fires when the conflicting annotation is actually present. I also want to confirm createMockFor returns null regardless of what arguments are passed in, and that process() correctly iterates across multiple fields.

I should note assertNoAnnotations is package-private so the test can call it directly since it's in the same package. I also need to verify the actual signature of unsupportedCombinationOfAnnotations in Reporter to make sure the exception matches correctly.

Checking Reporter's method, it likely throws a MockitoException directly rather than returning anything, so calling it inside assertNoAnnotations would propagate the exception upward through process() as well. I should test this with an expected MockitoException, plus verify edge cases like a null instance field and multiple undesired annotations passed as varargs.

I'm also thinking about whether static final fields with object construction could get compile-time inlined, but since they're not primitives or constant Strings, they won't be folded by the compiler, so reflection-based field manipulation should still work as intended.

Regardless of initializer, the reflection restriction on final fields applies based purely on modifiers, so setting a static final field should throw IllegalAccessException as expected. I want to confirm that process() wraps this exception with a message like "Problems initiating spied field " plus the field name, and that field.get ignores the instance parameter for static fields.

For the test case, I need the static field to hold a non-mock instance so it falls into the branch that calls field.set with a spy, triggering the exception. I should also verify that when @Mock and @Spy are both present, the conflict check runs before any field access, so the field's initial value doesn't matter in that scenario.

Now I'm setting up the test class structure with the engine instance and planning the static nested fixture classes needed for the Spy, Mock, and Captor combination tests.

Adding test methods covering: null return from createMockFor, no fields present, fields without the Spy annotation being skipped, valid instance spy creation, null instance throwing an exception, resetting an existing mock instead of spying, and expecting MockitoException for unsupported combinations with Mock and deprecated Mockito annotations.

Rounding out the test suite with cases for Captor annotation conflicts, static final field illegal access, the assertNoAnnotations helper with and without undesired annotations, empty varargs, and a mixed-field test that exercises multiple loop branches together. I still need to verify the actual field.get behavior.

I'm reasoning through the IllegalArgumentException case: the test instance passed to process() must actually be an instance of the declaring class for the field being accessed, so I need fixture classes set up accordingly with the context class matching the fixture's type. I'll define static nested fixture classes with various fields, then write assertions verifying the processed values for each field in the mixed test.

Next I need to test the null spy case, where a field annotated @Spy is null -- processing should throw a MockitoException with a message mentioning "Cannot create a @Spy". I also need a case where the spy field is already assigned a mock, so I can verify that process() calls Mockito.reset on it by checking interactions before and after processing.

For a simpler approach, I'll stub a method on the mock, confirm the stubbed value before processing, then confirm it reverts to the default value after processing -- proving reset was invoked. Finally, for the valid spy creation test, I'll verify the field gets wrapped into an actual spy of its original value.

Exact structural checks should suffice without worrying about deep copy behavior from the spy.

Now I'm setting up the static final field test case with a `@Spy static final List` field, expecting the engine to throw a MockitoException with a "Problems initiating spied field" message, since Field#set should reject final static fields even with setAccessible(true).

Since get() still works for reading, and the instance isn't a mock, the code falls into the field.set() branch which throws IllegalAccessException, getting wrapped as MockitoException — matching expectations. I also plan to write assertNoAnnotations tests, invoking the package-private method directly since the test class lives in the same package.

I also need to add the LinkedList import, then write small fixture classes with fields holding different annotation combinations (@Mock, none, @Captor) to exercise assertNoAnnotations. I'll test cases where no undesired annotations exist (no exception), where an undesired one is present (throws), and where the varargs list is empty (always passes regardless of annotations).

I'm also planning a mixed-fields test with several fields covering annotated-spy, already-mock, and plain fields together, to ensure the loop correctly processes multiple fields in one call and exercises both branches of isAnnotationPresent. Writing fixture classes...
